title: Comprehensive Profiling of Plasma Fatty Acid Concentrations in Young Healthy Canadian Adults
finding: GC analysis of fatty acid methyl esters from total plasma lipids of 826 fasted healthy young Canadian adults quantified 61 fatty acids: mean oleate (18:1 c9) 1285.5 ± 416.7 µmol/l, cis-vaccenate (18:1 c11) 129.2 ± 59.5 µmol/l, and trans 18:1 isomers were measurable, for example elaidate (18:1 t9) 16.5 ± 11.3 µmol/l.

title: Carnitine Inborn Errors of Metabolism
finding: Review of human carnitine metabolism and its inborn errors: the biosynthetic substrate 6-N-trimethyllysine comes from lysosomal or proteasomal breakdown of proteins carrying N-methylated lysine residues, and is converted to carnitine by TMLD, HTMLA, TMABADH and BBD (BBOX1), with OCTN2 (SLC22A5) importing carnitine into cells. Normal plasma free carnitine is given as 25 to 50 micromolar, with over 99 percent of body carnitine intracellular.

title: The polar oxy-metabolome reveals the 4-hydroxymandelate CoQ10 synthesis pathway
finding: FLAG-tagged HPDL immunopurified from human cells formed 4-hydroxymandelate from 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate, but not from tyrosine or 4-hydroxyphenyllactate, and catalytically impaired HPDL mutants formed none; 4-HMA was the most highly 18O-labelled polar metabolite in human cell lines, and HPDL knockout lowered 13C9-tyrosine labelling of CoQ10 in dense cultures, with labelling restored only by wild-type HPDL.
locator: Results: HPDL makes 4-HMA from 4-HPPA; Fig. 2c-d, Fig. 3a

title: The DNA methyltransferase-like protein DNMT3L stimulates de novo methylation by Dnmt3a
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: DNMT3L has no conserved methyltransferase catalytic domain. Coexpressed in human cells with replicating minichromosomes carrying imprinting centers as targets, DNMT3L strongly stimulated de novo methylation by Dnmt3a at imprinted and nonimprinted sequences and at endogenous genomic sites, while coexpression with DNMT3B gave little or no change in target methylation.

title: Molecular basis of renal disease. Leukotrienes and lipoxins: lipoxygenase-derived modulators of leukocyte recruitment and vascular tone in glomerulonephritis
finding: Review of lipoxygenase products in glomerulonephritis which describes lipoxin formation only by successive oxygenation of arachidonic acid at carbon 15 and carbon 5 through an unstable 5,6-epoxytetraene, by platelet 12-lipoxygenase acting on neutrophil-derived LTA4, and by neutrophil 5-lipoxygenase acting on endothelial 15(R)-HETE after aspirin treatment; no conversion of 14,15-diHETE to lipoxin B4 appears anywhere in the text or in the pathway figure.

title: Albumin modifies the metabolism of hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acids via 12-lipoxygenase in human platelets
finding: In ionophore-activated human platelets in vitro, 12-lipoxygenase converted 5(S)-HETE into the 5(S),12(S)-dihydroxy product (identified by co-chromatography and UV spectra against synthetic standards) and 15(S)-HETE into the 14(R),15(S)-dihydroxy product; 600 micromolar albumin cut formation of the first by roughly 90 percent while raising formation of the second about 7-fold, and it also lifted the inhibition that 15(S)-HETE exerted on 12(S)-HETE synthesis from endogenous arachidonate. Equilibrium dialysis with Scatchard analysis gave albumin binding constants of about 1.8e5 for 15-HETE, 1.4e5 for 12-HETE and 0.9e5 for 5-HETE.
locator: Results, Albumin influence on 5-HETE metabolism (Figs. 1, 2) and Albumin influence on the metabolism of 15-HETE by platelets (Figs. 4, 5); Results, Albumin binding of hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid

title: Activity of human Δ5 and Δ6 desaturases on multiple n‐3 and n‐6 polyunsaturated fatty acids
finding: In yeast co-expressing human desaturase and elongase genes, a single human delta-5 desaturase (FADS1) desaturated 20:3n-6 and 20:4n-3, and a single human delta-6 desaturase (FADS2) acted on 18:2n-6, 18:3n-3 and on the elongation-derived C24 substrates 24:4n-6 and 24:5n-3; activity was measured only in the heterologous yeast system with radiolabelled substrates.

title: Oxidative Inactivation of Human 5‐Lipoxygenase in Phosphatidylcholine Vesicles
finding: Human recombinant 5-lipoxygenase in phosphatidylcholine vesicles with Ca2+ oxygenated 12(S)-HETE, and the first-order inactivation rate of the enzyme during that reaction was about threefold lower than during arachidonic acid oxygenation (k(in) 0.6 per min for arachidonic acid). The oxygenation products of 12(S)-HETE were not identified.

title: Identification of the gene responsible for the cblB complementation group of vitamin B12-dependent methylmalonic aciduria
finding: MMAB on chromosome 12q24, found by searching bacterial genomes for adenosyltransferase-like genes next to the methylmalonyl-CoA mutase gene, encodes a predicted 250-residue protein with 45% similarity to the Salmonella cob(I)alamin adenosyltransferase PduO; deleterious mutations in cblB patient cell lines (R186W in four of six) identify it as the cblB gene. Function is inferred from sequence similarity, not measured.

title: Identification of the gene responsible for the cblA complementation group of vitamin B12-responsive methylmalonic acidemia based on analysis of prokaryotic gene arrangements
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: MMAA was identified as the gene of the cblA complementation group of B12-responsive methylmalonic acidemia: candidate selection from bacterial gene neighbourhoods of methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, followed by mutation analysis in cblA patient cell lines, found a 4-bp deletion in three lines plus an 8-bp insertion, a stop mutation and a missense change. The 418-residue product belongs to the AAA ATPase superfamily, and the authors propose only that it may be a transporter component or accessory protein for cobalamin entry into mitochondria; no transport was measured.

title: Carnitine biosynthesis by the perfused rat liver from exogenous protein-bound trimethyllysine. Metabolism of methylated lysine derivatives arising from the degradation of 6-N-[methyl-3H]lysine-labeled glycoproteins.
finding: Isolated rat livers were perfused with asialo-fetuin, asialo-orosomucoid or agalacto-orosomucoid whose lysine residues carried tritiated methyl groups: trimethylated glycoproteins were taken up and degraded, and the trimethyllysine set free was converted to 4-N-trimethylaminobutyrate, carnitine and O-acetylcarnitine, while the dimethylated glycoproteins yielded no appreciable carnitine or carnitine precursors and gave tritiated water and dimethyllysine instead. Which products accumulated depended on the receptor route, with 4-N-trimethylaminobutyrate building up in livers given the non-parenchymal substrate and acetylcarnitine dominating the medium with the parenchymal substrates.
locator: Abstract; Results: Metabolism of methylated lysine residues released in the perfused liver

title: Identification of DNMT1 (DNA methyltransferase 1) hypomorphs in somatic knockouts suggests an essential role for DNMT1 in cell survival
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Disruption of DNMT1 in human HCT116 cells produced a truncated DNMT1 protein lacking part of the regulatory N-terminal domain but retaining the catalytic C-terminal domain and hemimethylase activity; this protein was found, at different levels, in every DNMT1 knockout and DNMT1/DNMT3b double-knockout line examined, so these lines are hypomorphs rather than null.

title: Subcellular localization and physiological role of α-methylacyl-CoA racemase
finding: AMACR converts (2R)-methyl-branched acyl-CoAs to the (2S) isomers that beta-oxidation can degrade, and AMACR-deficient patients accumulate pristanic acid, DHCA and THCA in plasma. Subcellular fractionation of human and rat tissue shows the enzyme in both peroxisomes and mitochondria from one gene, and purified recombinant protein plus patient fibroblasts show the mitochondrial enzyme converts (2R,6)-dimethylheptanoyl-CoA to its (S) isomer.

title: Identification of the peroxisomal β-oxidation enzymes involved in the degradation of long-chain dicarboxylic acids
finding: Using fibroblasts from patients with defined mitochondrial and peroxisomal fatty acid oxidation defects, hexadecanedioic acid (C16DCA) was shown to be beta-oxidised in peroxisomes rather than mitochondria. Comparison of straight-chain acyl-CoA oxidase deficiency, D-bifunctional protein deficiency, X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy and rhizomelic chondrodysplasia punctata type 1 cells, plus assays of recombinant human L- and D-bifunctional protein expressed in a yeast fox2 deletion strain, identified ACOX1, both EHHADH and HSD17B4, and SCPx as the main enzymes, possibly with the classic 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase; shown for C16DCA only.

title: A novel case of ACOX2 deficiency leads to recognition of a third human peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidase
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Molecular Basis of Disease
finding: In a newly identified ACOX2-deficient patient, plasma C27 bile acid intermediates were raised and ACOX2 protein was absent on immunoblot, yet pristanic acid oxidation in fibroblasts was normal; substrate specificity tests of ACOX1, ACOX2 and ACOX3 assigned straight-chain fatty acids to ACOX1, bile acid synthesis to ACOX2 alone, and branched-chain fatty acid degradation to both ACOX2 and ACOX3, with ACOX3 mRNA and protein detected in normal human tissues.

title: A novel case of ACOX2 deficiency leads to recognition of a third human peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidase
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Molecular Basis of Disease
finding: Substrate specificity studies of human ACOX1, ACOX2 and ACOX3 placed ACOX2 as the sole human acyl-CoA oxidase in bile acid synthesis, while ACOX1 handles straight-chain fatty acids and both ACOX2 and ACOX3 act on branched-chain fatty acids. A new ACOX2-deficient patient had raised plasma C27-bile acid intermediates with no detectable ACOX2 protein but normal pristanic acid oxidation in fibroblasts, and ACOX3 expression was detected in normal human tissues.

title: A novel case of ACOX2 deficiency leads to recognition of a third human peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidase
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Molecular Basis of Disease
finding: Substrate specificity studies of human ACOX1, ACOX2 and ACOX3 show that ACOX1 oxidises straight-chain acyl-CoAs of different chain lengths, ACOX2 is the only one acting in bile acid synthesis, and ACOX2 and ACOX3 both degrade branched-chain acyl-CoAs; prompted by an ACOX2-deficient patient with normal pristanic acid oxidation in fibroblasts.

title: Mechanisms in anti-inflammation and resolution: the role of lipoxins and aspirin-triggered lipoxins
journal: Brazilian Journal of Medical and Biological Research
finding: Review of lipoxins and aspirin-triggered lipoxins which sets out three transcellular routes to lipoxin A4 and lipoxin B4, namely 15-lipoxygenase products of airway epithelial cells or monocytes converted by neutrophil 5-lipoxygenase via a 5S,6S,15S-epoxytetraene, LTA4 passed from myeloid cells to platelet 12-lipoxygenase, and acetylated COX-2-derived 15R-HETE converted by leukocyte 5-lipoxygenase to the 15-epimer lipoxins; no formation of lipoxin B4 from 14,15-diHETE is described.

title: Structures of the Human GTPase MMAA and Vitamin B12-dependent Methylmalonyl-CoA Mutase and Insight into Their Complex Formation
finding: Crystal structures of human MMAA with GDP and of human methylmalonyl-CoA mutase in apo, holo and substrate-bound ternary forms show conserved domains but a different dimeric assembly from the bacterial proteins; MMAA has GTPase activity modulated by the mutase, stable complex formation needs GMPPNP rather than GDP and the mutase apoenzyme, and the patient mutation MMAA G188R keeps basal GTPase activity while losing the interaction. The gatekeeping role in adenosylcobalamin loading and holoenzyme release is the authors' interpretation.

title: Differences in the Serum Nonesterified Fatty Acid Profile of Young Women Associated with a Recent History of Gestational Diabetes and Overweight/Obesity
finding: LC-MS/MS quantification of 41 serum NEFA species in fasting sera of 111 young women (62 post-gestational diabetes, 49 controls) gave group median molar percentages of 25.1 and 25.6 for 16:0, 39.5 and 39.1 for 18:1, 11.1 and 10.4 for 18:2 and 8.5 and 9.0 for 18:0, with trace species quantified down to 0.050 percent for 19:0, 0.005 percent for 24:6 and 0.006 percent for 26:1.
locator: Results: Serum NEFA composition in women after GDM and controls; Table 3

title: A bacterial light response reveals an orphan desaturase for human plasmalogen synthesis
finding: The Myxococcus xanthus enzyme CarF has the plasmanylethanolamine desaturase activity that forms the plasmalogen vinyl ether bond; its human homolog TMEM189 (PEDS1) replaces CarF function in M. xanthus, and TMEM189 knockout in a human cell line abolished plasmalogens.

title: Navigating the B12 Road: Assimilation, Delivery, and Disorders of Cobalamin
finding: Minireview of mammalian cobalamin uptake, lysosomal release, cytosolic processing by CblC and delivery to methionine synthase and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase. In its closing Summary the review lists the mitochondrial membrane transporters that bring cobalamin into the mitochondrion as not yet identified (as is the reductase partner of ATR), and the Figure 2 model marks this transporter with a question mark.

title: A randomized comparison between rasburicase and allopurinol in children with lymphoma or leukemia at high risk for tumor lysis
finding: Randomized trial in 52 children with leukemia or lymphoma at high risk of tumor lysis: recombinant urate oxidase (rasburicase) gave a mean plasma uric acid AUC over the first 96 hours of 128 +/- 70 mg/dL.hour against 329 +/- 129 mg/dL.hour for allopurinol (p < 0.0001), and an 86% against 12% fall in uric acid four hours after the first dose. Urate oxidase is given here as a recombinant drug; the paper reports no endogenous human urate oxidase activity or allantoin formation.

title: Methylation of tRNAAsp by the DNA Methyltransferase Homolog Dnmt2
finding: Human DNMT2 showed no DNA methylation activity; its substrate was a small RNA, identified by mass spectrometry as tRNA-Asp, specifically at cytosine 38 in the anticodon loop. Human DNMT2 protein also restored tRNA-Asp methylation in vitro to tRNA from Dnmt2-deficient mouse, Arabidopsis thaliana and Drosophila melanogaster, depending on preexisting nucleoside modifications.

title: Coordination Chemistry Controls Coenzyme B12 Synthesis by Human Adenosine Triphosphate:Cob(I)alamin Adenosyltransferase
finding: In vitro, NADPH with FDXR and FDX1 (adrenodoxin) reduces MMAB-bound cob(II)alamin and supports adenosylcobalamin synthesis (kcat 4.7 min-1, 2.5-fold below titanium(III) citrate; Km for FDX1 135 nM), and no AdoCbl forms without FDX1 or FDXR. The 4-coordinate cob(II)alamin reduction potential is -325 ± 9 mV (measured on the R190H variant); the authors call FDX1 a potential MMAB redox partner.

title: Coordination Chemistry Controls Coenzyme B12 Synthesis by Human Adenosine Triphosphate:Cob(I)alamin Adenosyltransferase
finding: In the introduction, cited as prior work rather than tested here, methionine synthase reductase (MTRR) is described as able to supply electrons for AdoCbl synthesis in vitro, while being a cytoplasmic protein with no known effect of its deficiency on mitochondrial cobalamin metabolism. The paper's own measurements give a reduction potential of -325 +/- 9 mV for four-coordinate cob(II)alamin bound to human MMAB and identify the mitochondrial ferredoxin adrenodoxin (FDX1) as an electron donor that supports NADPH-dependent AdoCbl synthesis.

title: Strict Regiospecificity of Human Epithelial 15-Lipoxygenase-2 Delineates Its Transcellular Synthesis Potential
finding: Purified recombinant human 15-lipoxygenase-2 (ALOX15B) oxygenated both 5-HPETE and 5-HETE at C15 to 5,15-diH(P)ETE, with catalytic efficiencies of 31% and 25% of that for arachidonate, while 12-HPETE and 15-HPETE were not substrates and 5,15-diHPETE was not converted further to lipoxins. All measurements are in vitro with the purified enzyme.
locator: Results and Discussion: Steady-State Kinetics of 5-HPETE and Formation of the Lipoxin Intermediate 5,15-diHPETE; Table 1

title: Measurement of allantoin and uric acid in human body fluids. A potential index of free-radical reactions in vivo?
finding: The paper describes methods for measuring uric acid and allantoin in human body fluids and reports their concentrations in human serum and synovial fluid, and the authors suggest that changes in allantoin concentration may index free-radical reactions in vivo. That radical attack on uric acid yields allantoin is cited from earlier work, not shown here.

title: Generation and analysis of context-specific genome-scale metabolic models derived from single-cell RNA-Seq data
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: ftINIT builds context-specific models from pooled single-cell or bulk RNA-seq; with the mask used in this study, reactions without gene rules (spontaneous, exchange, transport and 52 custom reactions for protein generation and metabolite pooling) are left out of the optimization and always kept in the final model, except in the Metabolic Atlas models.

title: Crystallographic and Kinetic Studies of Human Mitochondrial Acetoacetyl-CoA Thiolase: The Importance of Potassium and Chloride Ions for Its Structure and Function,
finding: Kinetic measurements on human mitochondrial acetoacetyl-CoA thiolase (T2, ACAT1) show thiolytic degradation of acetoacetyl-CoA and of 2-methylacetoacetyl-CoA with comparable kcat/Km, and turnover numbers for both substrates rise about 3-fold when KCl goes from 0 to 40 mM. Crystal structures of the apo and CoA-bound forms locate the potassium site near the CoA and catalytic sites and attribute the 2-methyl-branched substrate tolerance to the Phe325-Pro326 dipeptide.

title: Dnmt3L cooperates with the Dnmt3 family of de novo DNA methyltransferases to establish maternal imprints in mice
finding: Dnmt3L, a Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b homolog without methyltransferase activity, is required in mice for establishing maternal methylation imprints and for correct expression of maternally imprinted genes; it interacts with Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b and co-localizes with them in transfected cell nuclei, and Dnmt3a-/- Dnmt3b+/- mice show the same failure of maternal imprinting. Dnmt3a and Dnmt3L are also required for spermatogenesis.

title: The Human Dnmt2 Has Residual DNA-(Cytosine-C5) Methyltransferase Activity
finding: Purified human DNMT2 showed weak DNA methyltransferase activity in two independent in vitro assays, with methylation at CG sites in a loose ttnCGga(g/a) consensus.

title: Photosynthesis of Previtamin D3 in Human Skin and the Physiologic Consequences
finding: In surgically obtained hypopigmented Caucasian skin, radiation in the 290 to 320 nm band converted 7-dehydrocholesterol into previtamin D3 across all epidermal strata and, to a lesser degree, the dermis, with the highest previtamin D3 content in stratum spinosum and stratum basale (Table 1). Previtamin D3 then rearranged into vitamin D3 by a temperature-driven, non-photochemical step (half-conversion at 28 h and 83 percent at equilibrium after 4 days at 37 C in methanol in vitro, half-conversion in 18 h and a 95:5 ratio by day 3 in rat skin in vivo); the authors argue against catalysis because incubations of previtamin D3 with plasma or skin homogenates followed the same time course as in methanol, and they attribute the faster in vivo rate to removal of vitamin D3 by the vitamin D-binding protein.
locator: Results and discussion paragraphs on cutaneous sites and thermal equilibration (Table 1; Fig. 1B; Fig. 2 scheme)

title: A general introduction to the biochemistry of mitochondrial fatty acid β‐oxidation
finding: Review of mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation: long-chain acyl-CoAs are handled by the membrane-bound VLCAD (ACADVL) and the trifunctional protein (HADHA and HADHB), which carries hydratase, long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase and thiolase activities, while medium- and short-chain intermediates are processed in the matrix by a separate set of soluble enzymes, crotonase (ECHS1), M/SCHAD (HADH) and MCKAT (ACAA2), all with broad specificity up to about ten carbons. Auxiliary enzymes are needed for unsaturated substrates, the enoyl-CoA isomerase (given as DCI, now ECI1) and DECR1.
locator: Biochemical basis of fatty acid oxidation: The beta-oxidation cycle; Fig. 1

title: Characterization of four mammalian 3‐hydroxyacyl‐CoA dehydratases involved in very long‐chain fatty acid synthesis
finding: All four human HACD proteins (HACD1 to HACD4) act as 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydratases, shown by rescue of growth in a PHS1 shut-off yeast strain and by in vitro assays with 3-hydroxypalmitoyl-CoA, not with a polyunsaturated intermediate; the four proteins differ in tissue expression and interact with the elongases ELOVL1 to ELOVL7 with some preferences.

title: SLC22A5 (OCTN2) Carnitine Transporter—Indispensable for Cell Metabolism, a Jekyll and Hyde of Human Cancer
finding: This review states that of the three plasma-membrane carnitine transporters, SLC22A5 (OCTN2) is the only high-affinity one that is ubiquitously expressed (Km 4.34 micromolar), SLC22A16 (CT2) also has high affinity (Km 20.3 micromolar) but is expressed mainly in testis and epididymis, and SLC6A14 transports carnitine with low affinity (Km 830 micromolar).

title: Fat-1 mice convert n-6 to n-3 fatty acids
finding: Transgenic mice carrying the C. elegans fat-1 n-3 desaturase convert n-6 to n-3 fatty acids, giving more n-3 and less n-6 fatty acids in organs and tissues without dietary n-3; the authors state as background that mammals cannot make n-3 from n-6 fatty acids.

title: The genomes of the South American opossum (Monodelphis domestica) and platypus (Ornithorhynchus anatinus) encode a more complete purine catabolic pathway than placental mammals
journal: Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology Part D: Genomics and Proteomics
finding: Genome searches in opossum (Monodelphis domestica) and platypus (Ornithorhynchus anatinus), compared with 15 other vertebrates, found all six purine catabolic genes examined (XDH, UOX, 5-hydroxyisourate hydrolase, OHCU decarboxylase, allantoinase and allantoicase), including the allantoinase gene that is absent from placental mammal genomes; Ka/Ks values of 0.07 to 0.47 are consistent with purifying selection on all six. No allantoinase remnant was found at the expected syntenic position in placental genomes, so the loss is specific to placental mammals.
locator: Results: The opossum and platypus genomes encode a more complete set of genes for purine catabolism than do placental mammals; Fig. 2 and Table 1

title: The Evolutionary Fate of the Genes Encoding the Purine Catabolic Enzymes in Hominoids, Birds, and Reptiles
finding: Comparative genomic analysis of five hominoids, two birds and one reptile found that in hominoids the loss of urate oxidase is accompanied by genetic deterioration of the immediately downstream purine catabolic genes, while in birds and reptiles the UOX locus itself and some downstream genes are present and predicted to encode proteins. The explanation offered for the different outcomes, retention through new or alternative functions, is the authors' hypothesis.

title: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy: Very long-chain fatty acid metabolism, ABC half-transporters and the complicated route to treatment
finding: This review states that X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy is caused by mutations in ABCD1, encoding the peroxisomal ABC half-transporter ALDP, and that ALDP mutations raise very-long-chain fatty acid levels and reduce peroxisomal VLCFA beta-oxidation; it also notes that overexpression of the related half-transporter ALDRP corrects the biochemical defect in patient cells and in Abcd1 knockout mice.

title: The crystal structure of human mitochondrial 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase (T1): insight into the reaction mechanism of its thiolase and thioesterase activities
journal: Acta Crystallographica Section D Biological Crystallography
finding: Crystal structures of human mitochondrial T1 (ACAA2), apo and with CoA at 2.0 Å, show a tetramer; in solution T1 has low acyl-CoA thioesterase activity on fatty acyl-CoAs, fastest with butyryl-CoA, and significant biosynthetic (condensing) thiolase activity that the authors predict to be physiologically important.

title: Decyanation of vitamin B12 by a trafficking chaperone
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Human MMACHC (cblC) is shown to catalyse reductive decyanation of cyanocobalamin, using electrons passed from NADPH through cytosolic flavoprotein oxidoreductases to cleave the cobalt-carbon bond and release cyanide, giving base-off cob(II)alamin that can be assimilated into methylcobalamin and adenosylcobalamin. The authors relate this to cblC patient fibroblasts responding poorly to cyanocobalamin while showing partial metabolic correction with aquocobalamin.

title: MeaB Is a Component of the Methylmalonyl-CoA Mutase Complex Required for Protection of the Enzyme from Inactivation
finding: In Methylobacterium extorquens AM1, the growth defect of a meaB mutant comes from an inactive methylmalonyl-CoA mutase rather than from a lack of adenosylcobalamin, since double mutants blocked in R-methylmalonyl-CoA or adenosylcobalamin synthesis retain active mutase; purified MeaB forms a complex with the purified mutase and stimulates its activity in vitro, consistent with protection of the mutase from irreversible inactivation during catalysis.

title: Hepatic synthesis of carnitine from protein-bound trimethyl-lysine. Lysosomal digestion of methyl-lysine-labelled asialo-fetuin
finding: Asialo-fetuin labelled in its lysine methyl groups was cleared from rat blood by the liver and hydrolysed within hepatocyte lysosomes; the methylated lysines released there moved out of the lysosomes into the cytosol, where they were metabolised further. At least 34.6 percent of the protein-bound trimethyllysine was converted into carnitine within 3 hours in vivo, and 30 percent within 90 minutes in isolated perfused rat liver, whereas no labelled carnitine was detected after injection of mono- and dimethyl-lysine-labelled protein.

title: Identification of the Human and Bovine ATP:Cob(I)alamin Adenosyltransferase cDNAs Based on Complementation of a Bacterial Mutant
finding: Human and bovine ATP:cob(I)alamin adenosyltransferase (MMAB) cDNAs, found by complementing an ATR-deficient bacterial strain, give 98 and 87 nmol/min/mg ATR activity when expressed in E. coli, and the human cDNA restores AdoCbl-dependent growth of the bacterial mutant on 1,2-propanediol; ATR protein is altered on western blots of cblB patient cell lines.

title: Human ATP:Cob(I)alamin Adenosyltransferase and Its Interaction with Methionine Synthase Reductase
finding: Purified recombinant human MMAB (ATP:cob(I)alamin adenosyltransferase) variants 239K and 239M had specific activities of 220 and 190 nmol per min per mg, with Km values of 6.3 and 6.9 micromolar for ATP and 1.2 and 1.6 micromolar for cob(I)alamin. In a reconstituted in vitro system, purified human methionine synthase reductase reduced cob(II)alamin to cob(I)alamin, which MMAB adenosylated to AdoCbl, with an optimum of about 4 MSR per ATR and evidence that the two proteins interact so the cob(I)alamin intermediate is sequestered.

title: Cloning of a human cDNA encoding a novel enzyme involved in the elongation of long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids
finding: A human liver cDNA, HELO1 (ELOVL5), encoding a 299-residue protein with a histidine-rich domain, elongated polyunsaturated fatty acids when expressed in Saccharomyces cerevisiae: 18:3n-6 to 20:3n-6, 20:4n-6 to 22:4n-6, 18:4n-3 to 20:4n-3, 20:5n-3 to 22:5n-3 and 18:3n-3 to 20:3n-3, with highest mRNA in adrenal gland and testis. No reduction or retroconversion of docosahexaenoic acid is reported.

title: Identification and expression of mammalian long‐chain PUFA elongation enzymes
finding: Human ELOVL2 (296 residues) and mouse Elovl2 (292 residues) expressed in Saccharomyces cerevisiae elongated C20 and C22 PUFA, converting 20:4n-6 to 22:4n-6, 22:4n-6 to 24:4n-6, 20:5n-3 to 22:5n-3 and 22:5n-3 to 24:5n-3; mouse Elovl2 expressed in mouse L cells incubated with C20 and C22 substrates raised 24:4n-6 and 24:5n-3 levels.

title: Glutathione-dependent One-electron Transfer Reactions Catalyzed by a B12 Trafficking Protein
finding: Purified human CblC (MMACHC) catalyses glutathione-dependent decyanation of cyanocobalamin and reduction of aquacobalamin to cob(II)alamin, efficiently only under anaerobic conditions; the C. elegans enzyme also performs both reactions. In vitro only.

title: Structure of the human signal peptidase complex reveals the determinants for signal peptide cleavage
finding: Electron cryo-microscopy and structural proteomics gave atomic structures of two paralogous forms of the human ER signal peptidase complex, differing in the proteolytic subunit (SEC11A or SEC11C), which cleave signal peptides from secretory pre-proteins. The active site, formed by a catalytic triad, sits next to a transmembrane window where the subunits thin the bilayer locally, and molecular dynamics indicates specificity set by the length of the signal peptide hydrophobic segment.

title: Knockout of Tmlhe in mice is not associated with autism spectrum disorder phenotypes or motor dysfunction despite low carnitine levels
finding: Mice with constitutive inactivation of the Tmlhe-encoded trimethyllysine dioxygenase had carnitine reduced by more than 90% against wild type, together with very low gamma-butyrobetaine, yet showed no autism-associated social, cognitive or repetitive-behaviour changes, unchanged muscle strength and coordination, and a life expectancy similar to wild type.

title: The Biosynthesis of A2E, a Fluorophore of Aging Retina, Involves the Formation of the Precursor, A2-PE, in the Photoreceptor Outer Segment Membrane
finding: All-trans-retinal reacted with dipalmitoyl-phosphatidylethanolamine without an enzyme to give A2-PE, confirmed by UV and by mass spectrometry (m/z 1222.9, product ion m/z 672.8); A2-PE was also detected in retinal plus photoreceptor outer segment mixtures and in Royal College of Surgeons rat retina, and incubation of such mixtures with phospholipase D released A2E, which identifies A2-PE as the A2E precursor.

title: Carnitine transport and fatty acid oxidation
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Molecular Cell Research
finding: Review: normal circulating carnitine is 25-50 µM (0-8 µM in primary carnitine deficiency); cells accumulate carnitine and kidneys reabsorb it through the high-affinity carnitine transporter OCTN2 (SLC22A5), and inborn errors of carnitine synthesis usually leave plasma carnitine normal.

title: Double Bond Removal from Odd-numbered Carbons during Peroxisomal β-Oxidation of Arachidonic Acid Requires both 2,4-Dienoyl-CoA Reductase and Δ3,5,Δ2,4-Dienoyl-CoA Isomerase
finding: Incubating clofibrate-induced rat liver peroxisomes with [1-14C]4,7,10-hexadecatrienoate gave 2-trans-4,7,10-hexadecatetraenoate plus two isomers carrying a conjugated triene (UV maxima at 257, 267 and 277 nm) that the authors assign as 3,5,7,10-hexadecatetraenoate, and the matching accumulation of 2-trans-4,8,11,14-eicosapentaenoate from arachidonate without NADPH led them to conclude that removal of the odd-numbered double bonds of arachidonate needs NADPH-dependent 2,4-dienoyl-CoA reductase together with a delta-3,5,delta-2,4-dienoyl-CoA isomerase acting in the reverse direction.
locator: Results (Fig. 2 radiochromatograms, Figs. 4 and 5 UV spectra) and Discussion with the proposed pathway (Fig. 8)

title: Structural basis of signal peptide recognition by the signal peptidase complex
finding: A 2.6 Angstrom cryo-EM map of human SPC-A bound to a model signal peptide shows the c-region of the peptide in a hydrophobic luminal groove next to the active site, a narrow gate at the transition from c-region to h-region, and the h-region in a transmembrane window; substrate binding stabilises the N- and C-terminal helices of SEC11A that are unresolved in the apo structure. Molecular dynamics and AlphaFold modelling support this binding mode.

title: Integration of clinical data with a genome‐scale metabolic model of the human adipocyte
finding: iAdipocytes1809 builds its lipid pool reactions from published fatty acid compositions, with plasma non-esterified fatty acids from a fasting human plasma lipidomics study that reported 31 fatty acids; fatty acids absent from that study were assigned half the lowest reported concentration. In Supplementary Dataset 8 the plasma NEFA column lists 59 fatty acids, 31 with measured values summing to 214.3 nmol/ml and the other 28 marked as not reported and given the normalised value 9e-6.
locator: Results: Reconstruction of the adipocytes GEM iAdipocytes1809; Supplementary Dataset 8 (msb20135-s12.xlsx)

title: Genome-scale metabolic modelling of hepatocytes reveals serine deficiency in patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
finding: HMR 2.0 (8,181 reactions, 6,007 metabolites, 3,765 genes) extends lipid metabolism with 59 individual fatty acids in place of a generic fatty acid pool, and the hepatocyte model iHepatocytes2322 built from it (7,930 reactions, 2,322 genes) uses the same 59 fatty acids.

title: Architecture of the human G-protein-methylmalonyl-CoA mutase nanoassembly for B12 delivery and repair
finding: A crystal structure of the human MMUT-MMAA assembly (two MMUT chains with two MMAA dimers) shows the MMUT B12 domain rotated about 180 degrees relative to free MMUT and exposed to solvent, with MMAA wedged between the substrate and B12 domains and the interconnecting belt partially disordered. Methylmalonic aciduria mutations at the interfaces (MMUT R228Q, R616C, R694W; MMAA R98G, R209S) reduce MMUT-stimulated GTPase activation and MMAA-gated AdoCbl transfer, supporting the relevance of the structure.
locator: Results: MMUT in the M2C2 complex; Fig. 3A

title: Identification of ABC transporters acting in vitamin B 12 metabolism in Caenorhabditis elegans
finding: A screen of 37 Caenorhabditis elegans ABC transporter mutants for methylmalonic acid excretion identified wht-6, which excreted more methylmalonic acid and incorporated less 14C-propionate while cystathionine excretion stayed normal, and the excretion was partly corrected by vitamin B12 in the medium; the authors propose wht-6, whose human ortholog belongs to the ABCG family, as a candidate mitochondrial cobalamin importer, the gene for which is not known.

title: Urate as a Physiological Substrate for Myeloperoxidase
finding: Myeloperoxidase with hydrogen peroxide oxidised urate to 5-hydroxyisourate, which decayed mainly to allantoin; urate reduced MPO compound I and compound II with rate constants of 4.6e5 and 1.7e4 per molar per second and competed with chloride, and stimulated neutrophils in human plasma produced allantoin in an NADPH oxidase, MPO and superoxide dependent reaction.

title: Lecithin Retinol Acyltransferase Contains Cysteine Residues Essential for Catalysis
finding: LRAT from human retinal pigment epithelium is highly sensitive to thiol-directed reagents; C161A and C168A mutants are virtually inactive, C182A and C208A keep most activity, and C161S retains a few percent with an aberrant pH-rate profile, so the authors conclude LRAT is a thiol acyltransferase with C161 as the likely nucleophile.

title: Identification of Two Mammalian Reductases Involved in the Two-carbon Fatty Acyl Elongation Cascade
finding: Two mammalian enzymes of the microsomal fatty acyl elongation cycle were identified and characterised: the 3-ketoacyl-CoA reductase and the trans-2,3-enoyl-CoA reductase, acting in long- and very-long-chain elongation respectively. The abstract names no gene symbols; UniProt assigns these activities to HSD17B12 (Q53GQ0, EC 1.1.1.330) and TECR (Q9NZ01, EC 1.3.1.93), citing this paper as experimental evidence.

title: In vitro construction of the COQ metabolon unveils the molecular determinants of coenzyme Q biosynthesis
finding: Using ancestral sequence reconstruction to obtain soluble enzymes, the authors assembled the animal COQ biosynthetic pathway in vitro, assigned enzymes to steps that had been uncharacterised, and showed that the kinase COQ8 increases and streamlines coenzyme Q production in that reconstituted system.

title: Loss of Urate Oxidase Activity in Hominoids and its Evolutionary Implications
finding: Sequencing of the Uox promoter, coding and intronic regions across primates confirmed that the gene is inactivated in humans and great apes by a single shared CGA to TGA nonsense mutation in exon 2, whereas the gibbon lineage was inactivated independently by a nonsense mutation at a different exon 2 CGA codon or by frameshifts in exon 3 or exon 5; substitutions in the CAAT box of functional primate Uox genes may also lower transcription.

title: ELOVL1 production of C24 acyl-CoAs is linked to C24 sphingolipid synthesis
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Membranes of HEK293T cells overexpressing each human ELOVL1-7 were assayed with [14C]malonyl-CoA and 11 acyl-CoAs (C16:0 to C26:0, C18 PUFAs, 20:4n-6): ELOVL1 elongated saturated C18:0-C26:0 (highest on C22:0) and none of the unsaturated substrates tested; ELOVL2 and ELOVL5 acted only on PUFA (most active on 20:4n-6 and 18:3n-6); ELOVL4 weakly on C24:0 and C26:0. No C22 PUFA was tested.
locator: Results: Determination of Substrate Specificities of ELOVL Proteins; Fig. 1B

title: Dnmt2 is not required for de novo and maintenance methylation of viral DNA in embryonic stem cells
finding: Mouse Dnmt2, cloned as a homolog of fission yeast pmt1 and containing the conserved methyltransferase motifs, showed no DNA methylation activity as a baculovirus-expressed protein in vitro. In ES cells where the catalytic PPC motif was deleted by targeting, endogenous virus DNA remained fully methylated and newly integrated retroviral DNA was methylated de novo as efficiently as in wild type, so Dnmt2 is dispensable for genome-wide de novo and maintenance methylation in these cells.

title: A G-protein editor gates coenzyme B12 loading and is corrupted in methylmalonic aciduria
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: With purified components, the G protein MeaB uses GTP binding to discriminate active from inactive cobalamin forms and GTP hydrolysis to gate transfer of adenosylcobalamin from adenosyltransferase to methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, and also elicits release of inactive cofactor formed during turnover; a patient mutation in methylmalonyl-CoA mutase leaves the enzyme's own activity intact but corrupts cofactor loading fidelity and ejection, giving accumulation of inactive enzyme.

title: Mechanistic Details of Early Steps in Coenzyme Q Biosynthesis Pathway in Yeast
finding: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Hfd1 oxidises 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde to 4-hydroxybenzoate for coenzyme Q synthesis, and HFD1 inactivation caused Q deficiency that was rescued by expression of human ALDH3A1; the authors propose that an equivalent pathway operates in animals.

title: COQ4 is required for the oxidative decarboxylation of the C1 carbon of coenzyme Q in eukaryotic cells
finding: COQ4 catalyses the C1 decarboxylation and hydroxylation of CoQ precursors as one oxidative decarboxylation: COQ4-knockout HEK293 cells make no CoQ10 and accumulate the COQ2 product 3-decaprenyl-4-hydroxybenzoate, COQ4 complements an E. coli strain lacking these steps, and COQ4 forms polyprenyl-benzoquinone in C. glutamicum. No in vitro assay with purified COQ4 is reported.

title: Role of Human 15-Lipoxygenase-2 in the Biosynthesis of the Lipoxin Intermediate, 5S,15S-diHpETE, Implicated with the Altered Positional Specificity of Human 15-Lipoxygenase-1
finding: With purified recombinant human lipoxygenases, oxygenation of 12S-HETE and 15S-HETE by 5-lipoxygenase was kinetically slow, so the authors conclude that 5S-HETE is the first intermediate in the in vitro biosynthesis of both 5S,12S-diHETE and 5S,15S-diHETE. 15-lipoxygenase-1 acting on 5S-HETE gave 90 percent 5S,12S-diHETE with kinetics 5-fold greater than 12-lipoxygenase, while 15-lipoxygenase-2 gave 5S,15S-diHETE with a kcat/Km flux twice that of 15-lipoxygenase-1.

title: The suppression of 5-lipoxygenation of arachidonic acid in human polymorphonuclear leucocytes by the 15-lipoxygenase product (15S)-hydroxy-(5Z,8Z,11Z,13E)-eicosatetraenoic acid: structure-activity relationship and mechanism of action
finding: In ionophore A23187-stimulated human polymorphonuclear leucocytes, 15-[14C]HETE was converted to labelled 5S,15S-diHETE, and the same conversion was obtained with purified human recombinant 5-lipoxygenase; 15-HETE therefore suppresses 5-lipoxygenation of arachidonate by competing as a substrate rather than by inhibiting the enzyme, and 5,15-diHETE formation in the cells was stimulated by hydroperoxy fatty acids or arachidonate.

title: Biological Inactivation of 5-oxo-6,8,11,14-Eicosatetraenoic Acid by Human Platelets
finding: A23187-stimulated mixtures of human platelets and neutrophils produced two 12-hydroxylated derivatives of 5-oxo-ETE in large amounts, 5-oxo-12-HETE and 8-trans-5-oxo-12-HETE, identified by comparison with chemically synthesised standards; platelets stimulated with thrombin or A23187 also formed them from 5-oxo-ETE, while unstimulated platelets converted 5-oxo-ETE mainly to 5-HETE.

title: Lipidomics reveals a remarkable diversity of lipids in human plasma
finding: Mass-spectrometric lipidomics of NIST SRM 1950, plasma pooled from 100 fasted adults aged 40 to 50 with an ethnic and sex distribution matching the US population, gave a total of 214 nmol/ml of non-esterified fatty acids across 31 quantified species, of which oleate, palmitate and stearate together accounted for roughly 78 percent, linoleate plus arachidonate for roughly 8 percent, and alpha-linolenate, EPA and DHA together for roughly 1 percent.
locator: Results and Discussion: Fatty acyls; Table 1 and supplementary Table IA

title: Completing the uric acid degradation pathway through phylogenetic comparison of whole genomes
finding: Phylogenetic genome comparison identified two genes sharing the loss and gain pattern of urate oxidase, and the two mouse proteins were shown to catalyse the steps after urate oxidation: hydrolysis of 5-hydroxyisourate to OHCU, and decarboxylation of OHCU to S-(+)-allantoin. Urate oxidase alone gives racemic allantoin over hours, whereas the three enzymes together give dextrorotatory allantoin within seconds.

title: Isolation and sequence determination of a cDNA clone for rat peroxisomal urate oxidase: liver-specific expression in the rat.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: A 1.3 kb rat liver cDNA clone covering 97% of the urate oxidase coding region was isolated and its identity confirmed by fusion protein analysis, epitope-selected antibody localization to peroxisomes and peptide sequence comparison; a single 1.5 kb mRNA was detected in rat liver and a hepatocellular carcinoma but in none of 11 non-hepatic tissues, the gene is present in a single copy, and no urate oxidase mRNA was found in human liver.

title: CpG methylation is maintained in human cancer cells lacking DNMT1
finding: Human HCT116 colorectal carcinoma cells with DNMT1 disrupted by homologous recombination had markedly lower cellular DNA methyltransferase activity but only a 20 percent decrease in overall genomic methylation; juxtacentromeric satellites were significantly demethylated while most loci analysed, including p16INK4a, stayed fully methylated and silenced.

title: DNMT1 and DNMT3b cooperate to silence genes in human cancer cells
finding: In a human colorectal cancer cell line, deleting DNMT3B reduced total genomic methylation by under 3%, while the DNMT1 plus DNMT3B double knockout lost almost all DNA methyltransferase activity and lowered genomic methylation by more than 95%.

title: An atlas of human metabolism
finding: In the Human1 (Human-GEM) gene essentiality analysis, a gene counts as essential if its deletion impairs any of 57 basic metabolic tasks, biomass production among them, rather than growth alone; the authors state this reduces dependence on the biomass reaction formulation and hypothesise higher sensitivity. Predictions were made on five cell-line-specific models built with tINIT from CRISPR-screened cell lines (GBM, RPE1, HCT116, DLD1, HeLa) and compared with HMR2 and Recon3D.
locator: Results: Prediction of metabolic task-essential genes in human cell lines; Fig. 4A

title: Structural conservation, functional decline: The fate of human OHCU decarboxylase
finding: Recombinant human OHCU decarboxylase (URAD) is a well-folded alpha-helical protein closely similar to the zebrafish enzyme (52% sequence identity, RMSD below 0.8 Angstrom) but less stable, and in functional assays its catalytic activity is markedly lower than that of the zebrafish enzyme; molecular dynamics indicates different ligand binding and altered conformational flexibility in the human protein.

title: Sterol carrier protein X is peroxisomal 3-oxoacyl coenzyme A thiolase with intrinsic sterol carrier and lipid transfer activity.
finding: Purified recombinant SCPx cleaved 3-oxoacyl(n)-CoA to acetyl-CoA plus acyl(n-2)-CoA, stimulated microsomal conversion of 7-dehydrocholesterol to cholesterol and transferred phosphatidylcholine and 7-dehydrocholesterol between membranes in vitro, and SCPx epitopes were detected mainly in peroxisomes, which identifies SCPx as a peroxisomal 3-oxoacyl-CoA thiolase with intrinsic sterol carrier and lipid transfer activity. The abstract gives no acyl chain lengths and does not name the species.

title: Coenzyme Q headgroup intermediates can ameliorate a mitochondrial encephalopathy
finding: Hpdl-/- mice (untreated pups die by P15) incorporated orally given 13C6-4-hydroxymandelate or 13C6-4-hydroxybenzoate into brain CoQ9 and CoQ10, and 10 mg/kg/day from P3-P5 to P30 let 90-100% reach adulthood, whereas CoQ9 or CoQ10 supplementation did not; 4-HB also stabilised symptoms in one patient with biallelic HPDL variants.

title: DNMT3L Stimulates the DNA Methylation Activity of Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b through a Direct Interaction
finding: In vitro, human DNMT3L raised the DNA methylation activity of mouse Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b 1.5- to 3-fold, increasing with the DNMT3L amount, without affecting Dnmt1, and the effect held for all DNA substrates tested, including imprinted loci, a CpG island and synthetic polynucleotides. DNMT3L bound Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b but not DNA, and the C-terminal half carried the stimulatory effect, so the authors attribute it to a direct action on catalytic activity rather than DNA targeting.

title: The acyl- and alkyl-glycerone phosphate reductase DHRS7 is involved in the production of distinct plasmalogen species from DHRS7B
finding: In human knockout and double-knockout cells, DHRS7 and DHRS7B both contribute to ethanolamine plasmalogen synthesis but to different species: DHRS7 contributes most to C18:1, then C16:0 and C22:4, while DHRS7B contributes to all species measured; DHRS7 localises to the endoplasmic reticulum and DHRS7B to peroxisomes, and in vitro DHRS7 shows both alkyl- and acyl-glycerone phosphate reductase activity, as DHRS7B does.

title: Protection and reactivation of human methylmalonyl-CoA mutase by MMAA protein
finding: With purified recombinant human proteins in vitro, MMAA added at the start of the reaction prevented inactivation of methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, and MMAA added after 60 minutes, when the mutase was inactive, raised activity again through GTP hydrolysis, consistent with exchange of the damaged cofactor; the mutase catalysed the reaction without MMAA, and the interaction was also seen in a yeast two-hybrid assay.

title: Molecular and Functional Identification of Sodium Ion-dependent, High Affinity Human Carnitine Transporter OCTN2
finding: Human OCTN2 (SLC22A5) expressed in HEK293 cells raised L-[3H]carnitine uptake in a sodium-dependent manner with Km 4.34 µM; tetraethylammonium and guanidine were poor substrates, and OCTN2 mRNA is strongly expressed in kidney, skeletal muscle, heart and placenta.

title: Human Metastasis Regulator Protein H-Prune is a Short-Chain Exopolyphosphatase
finding: Human h-prune (PRUNE1) hydrolyses short-chain polyphosphates with kcat of 3 to 40 per second, including inorganic tri- and tetrapolyphosphate and nucleoside 5'-tetraphosphates, while long-chain polyphosphates of 25 or more residues react more slowly and pyrophosphate and nucleoside triphosphates are not substrates. The activity needs a divalent metal (Mg, Co or Mn) and is suppressed by nm23-H1, long-chain polyphosphates and pyrophosphate; mutating residues matching the yeast exopolyphosphatase active site reduced activity.

title: Carnitine biosynthesis in mammals
finding: Review of mammalian carnitine biosynthesis stating that the pathway starts from trimethyllysine set free when methylated proteins are hydrolysed in lysosomes, that the aldolase cleaving 3-hydroxy-trimethyllysine may be serine hydroxymethyltransferase (cytosolic isoform the more likely candidate, on the basis of earlier work showing rabbit liver SHMT cleaves HTML, with the identity left unsettled), and that of the tissues assayed only kidney, liver and brain carry the full enzyme set because butyrobetaine dioxygenase is confined to them, so other tissues export butyrobetaine and take up carnitine from the circulation.
locator: Introduction and Figure 2B; HTMLA section; Tissue distribution of carnitine-biosynthetic enzymes and Figure 4

title: Substrate specificity of human carnitine acetyltransferase: Implications for fatty acid and branched-chain amino acid metabolism
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Molecular Basis of Disease
finding: Purified recombinant human CrAT converted short- and medium-chain acyl-CoAs (C2 to C10-CoA) into acylcarnitines quantified by ESI-MS/MS, with no activity on long-chain species, poor activity on trans-2-enoyl-CoA intermediates, activity on some but not all branched-chain amino acid oxidation intermediates, and no activity on dicarboxylic acyl-CoA esters; the abstract also states that CPT2 is inactive with short-chain and branched-chain intermediates.

title: A genome-wide atlas of co-essential modules assigns function to uncharacterized genes
finding: A co-essentiality atlas across CRISPR screens placed TMEM189 in an ether lipid synthesis module; HeLa-Cas9 cells with TMEM189-targeting sgRNAs had much lower levels of 37 plasmenylethanolamine (plasmalogen) species and higher levels of 30 plasmanylethanolamine precursor species, identifying TMEM189 as plasmanylethanolamine desaturase.
locator: Results: TMEM189 encodes the enzyme PEDS required for plasmalogen synthesis; Fig. 4c-e

title: Sterol Carrier Protein X (SCPx) Is a Peroxisomal Branched-Chain β-Ketothiolase Specifically Reacting with 3-Oxo-pristanoyl-CoA: A New, Unique Role for SCPx in Branched-Chain Fatty Acid Metabolism in Peroxisomes
finding: The conventional peroxisomal 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase reacted poorly with 3-oxoacyl-CoA esters of 2-methyl-branched fatty acids such as pristanic acid, whereas the 58 kDa SCPx protein, which has both thiolase and sterol carrier activity, readily cleaved 3-oxopristanoyl-CoA, placing SCPx in branched-chain fatty acid beta-oxidation in peroxisomes. The abstract does not state the species; UniProt cites this work as experimental evidence for rat SCPx (P11915).

title: Genetic dissection of polyunsaturated fatty acid synthesis in Caenorhabditis elegans
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Screening Caenorhabditis elegans by fatty acid composition yielded mutants defective in each desaturation and elongation step of the pathway from saturated precursors to arachidonic acid and eicosapentaenoic acid, and their compositions reveal the substrate preferences of the enzymes; n-3 and delta-5 unsaturated PUFA are not required for normal development under laboratory conditions, while mutants with more severe PUFA deficiency show growth and neurological defects.

title: The TMEM189 gene encodes plasmanylethanolamine desaturase which introduces the characteristic vinyl ether double bond into plasmalogens
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Mice homozygous for an inactivating Tmem189 knockout-first allele had kidney plasmanylethanolamine desaturase activity below the detection limit of 0.2 pmol per mg per min, had almost completely lost plasmalogens in kidney and in 12 other tissues, and had reduced body weight in both sexes (n = 3 per group); the mice reached adult phenotyping age.
locator: Results: Tmem189-Deficient Mice Lack Both PEDS Activity and Plasmalogens; Fig. 4

title: Synthesis, structural identification and biological activity of 11,12-dihydroxyeicosatetraenoic acids formed in human platelets
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Lipids and Lipid Metabolism
finding: Using synthetic standards (HPLC, GC, GC-MS), the main 11,12-diHETE made by human platelets is 11(R),12(S)-dihydroxy-5Z,7E,9E,14Z-eicosatetraenoic acid; the 11S,12S and 5E isomers are only tentatively identified. The authors propose formation via a leukotriene-like epoxide route, presumably by 12-lipoxygenase.

title: cDNA cloning, characterization, and tissue-specific expression of human xanthine dehydrogenase/xanthine oxidase.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: cDNAs for human xanthine dehydrogenase (EC 1.1.1.204) were isolated from a liver library and sequenced, giving a 1336-residue protein of about 148 kDa with a 2Fe/2S site and a putative molybdopterin domain, plus a proposed basis for conversion to xanthine oxidase; RNA blots found a 5100-base transcript in liver with tissue-specific distribution and a second 4500-base species in some tissues. The paper does not address urate oxidation or allantoin formation, the reactions it is cited for in the model.

title: Two independent mutational events in the loss of urate oxidase during hominoid evolution
finding: Sequencing of the urate oxidase gene in human, chimpanzee, orangutan and gibbon found nonsense mutations at codons 33 and 187 plus an aberrant splice site in human and chimpanzee, the codon 33 nonsense mutation in orangutan, and in gibbon instead a 13 bp deletion disrupting the reading frame, indicating two independent inactivation events after the gibbon lineage diverged.

title: Hyperuricemia and urate nephropathy in urate oxidase-deficient mice.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Mice with the urate oxidase gene disrupted by homologous recombination in embryonic stem cells developed pronounced hyperuricemia and urate nephropathy, and over 50 percent of the mutants died within their first 4 weeks, which the authors take to show that urate oxidase is essential in mice.

title: Resveratrol and para-coumarate serve as ring precursors for coenzyme Q biosynthesis
finding: Human and mouse cell lines, as well as E. coli and yeast, produced 13C6-labelled CoQ when fed 13C6-resveratrol or 13C6-coumarate, whereas E. coli and the mammalian cells did not make labelled CoQ from 13C6-pABA (unlike yeast). Isotope tracing only; no mammalian enzyme is identified.

title: Human methionine synthase reductase is a molecular chaperone for human methionine synthase
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Recombinant human methionine synthase and its reductase, purified from baculovirus-infected insect cells, showed that the reductase sustains methionine synthase activity at 1:1 stoichiometry with a Kact of 71 nM and stabilises the unstable apoenzyme, enhancing holoenzyme formation. The reductase also reduced aquacobalamin to cob(II)alamin with NADPH, which stimulated holoenzyme formation from apoenzyme plus aquacobalamin, leading the authors to propose a chaperone plus aquacobalamin reductase role.

title: ELOVL4 protein preferentially elongates 20:5n3 to very long chain PUFAs over 20:4n6 and 22:6n3
finding: In rat PC12 cells transduced with mouse Elovl4, with non-transduced and GFP-transduced cells as controls, only the ELOVL4-expressing cells made C28 to C38 very long chain PUFA, whereas controls, which carry endogenous Elovl1, Elovl2, Elovl4 message and abundant Elovl5 but no detectable ELOVL4 protein, elongated supplemented 20:5n-3, 22:6n-3 and 20:4n-6 to C22 to C26 products and formed 24:5n-3 as well, with 20:5n-3, 22:5n-3 and 24:5n-3 levels not differing significantly between ELOVL4 and control cells after 20:5n-3 supplementation; the authors ascribe this ELOVL4-independent elongation to endogenous ELOVL5 or ELOVL2.
locator: Results: Expression of ELOVL4 and elongation of supplemented FAs; Figs. 2A, 3A, 4A; Discussion

title: BBOX1 Deficiency Exacerbates Liver Fibrosis Through Carnitine Biosynthesis Disruption Rescued by Carnitine Supplementation
finding: Bbox1 knockout mice had profound hepatic carnitine depletion and, under thioacetamide challenge, developed worse liver fibrosis and inflammation than wild-type littermates, which the authors link to activation of TRPC6-Ca2+/CAMK2B signalling; dietary L-carnitine supplementation fully rescued the aggravated fibrotic phenotype. BBOX1 expression was also lower in human cirrhotic liver transcriptomes.

title: Identification of the peroxisomal β-oxidation enzymes involved in the degradation of leukotrienes
finding: Leukotriene beta-oxidation in peroxisomes needs D-bifunctional protein (HSD17B4); ALDP (ABCD1) and peroxisomal 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase (ACAA1) are not involved.

title: High-Resolution CRISPR Screens Reveal Fitness Genes and Genotype-Specific Cancer Liabilities
finding: CRISPR fitness screens in five human cell lines (DLD1, GBM, HCT116, HeLa, RPE1); the reference for Human-GEM's gene-essentiality test.

title: The Biosynthesis of Uroporphyrinogen III: Mechanism of Action of Porphobilinogen Deaminase
finding: Symposium review of how porphobilinogen deaminase builds the tetrapyrrole hydroxymethylbilane; it states that without the cosynthase (uroporphyrinogen III synthase) this product cyclises on its own to uroporphyrinogen I. The structural and mutagenesis parts concern the E. coli deaminase, and the spontaneous-cyclisation statement is a summary, not a new measurement.

title: Activation of human erythrocyte 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate phosphatase at physiological concentrations of substrate
finding: Enzyme-kinetic study of the purified human erythrocyte enzyme: in these cells the reactions of the 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate shunt are catalysed mainly by a single protein with synthase and phosphatase activity, and its phosphatase is activated by phosphate and sulfite, also at 5 mM 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate. In vitro with purified enzyme; the abstract does not name the gene.

title: NDUFA4 Is a Subunit of Complex IV of the Mammalian Electron Transport Chain
finding: Proteomic, genetic, evolutionary and biochemical analyses indicate that NDUFA4, formerly assigned to complex I, belongs to cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV): deleting NDUFA4 left complex I intact and affected complex IV function and assembly. The authors propose renaming the gene and treating it as a candidate for complex IV rather than complex I deficiency.

title: Expanding coincident signaling by PTEN through its inositol 1,3,4,5,6-pentakisphosphate 3-phosphatase activity
finding: PTEN purified after expression in bacteria or HEK cells removed the 3-phosphate of inositol 1,3,4,5,6-pentakisphosphate (Km 7.1 uM versus 26 uM for PtdIns(3,4,5)P3), and transient PTEN expression in HEK cells lowered the cellular level of this inositol phosphate. Contradicted in U87-MG cells by Orchiston 2004 (10.1074/jbc.m310933200), where wild-type PTEN did not change inositol phosphate levels.

title: The mechanism of formation of o-bromophenol from bromobenzene.
finding: In liver microsomes from 3-methylcholanthrene-treated rats, a bromobenzene 2,3-dihydrodiol was isolated and the deuterium label of o-bromophenol was largely retained, with no isotope effect; this indicates formation via bromobenzene-2,3-oxide rather than direct oxygen insertion. The authors state the result does not exclude oxygen addition followed by an NIH shift, and the abstract does not address spontaneous versus enzymatic isomerisation of the oxide.

title: Isolation and Sequencing of Salsolinol Synthase, an Enzyme Catalyzing Salsolinol Biosynthesis
finding: A 77-residue, 8.6 kDa ubiquitin-like protein was purified from rat brain and reported as salsolinol synthase; overexpression in eukaryotic cells raised salsolinol production over control. It makes salsolinol from dopamine and acetaldehyde in this system; no human gene is given.

title: 9-O-Acetylation of sialic acids is catalysed by CASD1 via a covalent acetyl-enzyme intermediate
finding: CRISPR/Cas knockout of CASD1 in human cells abolished sialic acid 9-O-acetylation, and the purified luminal domain moved acetyl groups from acetyl-CoA to CMP-activated sialic acid through a covalent acetyl-enzyme intermediate. The substrate shown is CMP-sialic acid, not a ganglioside.

title: Genetic evidence that the human CYP2R1 enzyme is a key vitamin D 25-hydroxylase
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: A patient with low circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D and vitamin D deficiency was homozygous for a CYP2R1 missense change (Leu99Pro) that removed vitamin D 25-hydroxylase activity. One patient; the paper identifies CYP2R1 as a relevant hepatic 25-hydroxylase.

title: Alpha-tocopheryl hydroquinone is an efficient multifunctional inhibitor of radical-initiated oxidation of low density lipoprotein lipids
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: In isolated human LDL, alpha-tocopheryl hydroquinone instantly reduced the lipoprotein's ubiquinone-10 to ubiquinol-10 and also scavenged radicals, acting as an antioxidant. In vitro on lipoprotein; the abstract does not mention an enzyme, so the reduction is non-enzymatic.

title: Stereoselective Formation and Metabolism of 4-Hydroxy-Retinoic Acid Enantiomers by Cytochrome P450 Enzymes
finding: Recombinant CYP26A1 formed mainly (4S)-4-hydroxy-retinoic acid, CYP3A4 formed both enantiomers equally, CYP3A5 favoured (4R), and CYP3A7 and CYP2C8 favoured (4S). CYP26A1 cleared (4S) about three times faster than (4R) and made 4-oxo-retinoic acid only from (4R); CYP26B1 and CYP26C1 are not tested in the abstract.

title: Evidence against Functionally Significant Aquaporin Expression in Mitochondria
finding: Mitochondrial membranes from rat brain, liver and kidney, and from wild-type and AQP-null mice, had similar osmotic water and glycerol permeabilities, and AQP8 was not detected by immunoblot in mouse liver mitochondria. The authors conclude aquaporins are not functionally significant there; H2O2 permeability was not measured.

title: Identities and Differences in the Metabolism of Tocotrienols and Tocopherols in HepG2 Cells
finding: In HepG2 cells alpha- and gamma-tocotrienol were degraded by omega- then beta-oxidation of the side chain to carboxychromanols; the intermediate with the original side-chain double bond (CMBHC) was not detected, so auxiliary enzymes as for unsaturated fatty acids are implied. One cell line; no genes tested.

title: Mutations in SRD5B1 (AKR1D1), the gene encoding delta(4)-3-oxosteroid 5beta-reductase, in hepatitis and liver failure in infancy
finding: Three infants with neonatal cholestatic liver disease whose main urinary and plasma bile acids were 3-oxo-delta4 species carried homozygous AKR1D1 (SRD5B1) mutations (two missense, one frameshift). Three patients; it describes the accumulating bile acids and not the order of steps in side-chain shortening.

title: Plasma Metanephrines Are Markers of Pheochromocytoma Produced by Catechol-O-Methyltransferase Within Tumors
journal: The Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism
finding: In pheochromocytoma patients, free metanephrines in tumour tissue exceeded plasma levels more than 10,000-fold, and over 93 percent of circulating metanephrines were calculated to come from catecholamine metabolism inside the tumour (COMT, mainly membrane-bound) before release. It does not test whether an ATP-driven export of normetanephrine exists.

title: Human carnitine biosynthesis proceeds via (2S,3S)-3-hydroxy-Nε-trimethyllysine
finding: Enzymatic and asymmetric chemical synthesis experiments define the product of trimethyllysine hydroxylase (TMLH, the first step of mammalian carnitine biosynthesis) as the (2S,3S) stereoisomer of 3-hydroxy-N-epsilon-trimethyllysine; the abstract does not report kinetics or a cell-based test.

title: Carnitine biosynthesis in mammals
organism: mammals (emphasis on Homo sapiens and Rattus norvegicus)
finding: Review of the enzymes, genes and regulation of mammalian carnitine biosynthesis. It leaves the submitochondrial site of trimethyllysine dioxygenase open and places most hydroxytrimethyllysine aldolase activity in the soluble fraction of human tissue, which makes a cytosolic isoenzyme more likely. This DOI string is an alternative form of the DOI 10.1042/bj3610417 of the same review.
locator: Review sections on trimethyllysine dioxygenase and hydroxytrimethyllysine aldolase (subcellular location)

title: Identification and Characterization of a Membrane Protein (y+L Amino Acid Transporter-1) That Associates with 4F2hc to Encode the Amino Acid Transport Activity y+L
finding: A cloned human cDNA (y+LAT-1) co-expressed with the 4F2 heavy chain (4F2hc) in Xenopus oocytes induced y+L amino acid transport and formed a disulfide-linked heterodimer with 4F2hc; mutating 4F2hc Cys109 abolished the heterodimer and sharply reduced transport. The mRNA is mainly in kidney, the gene maps to the lysinuric protein intolerance locus, and the authors propose it as a candidate gene; the abstract does not give per-substrate exchange specificity for the individual amino acid antiports.

title: The Molecular Architecture of Human N-Acetylgalactosamine Kinase
finding: Crystal structures of human GalNAc kinase (GALK2) with MnAMPPNP and GalNAc or with MgATP and GalNAc (bound products) place it in the GHMP kinase superfamily and define the determinants of GalNAc specificity; the abstract reports GalNAc as the substrate studied and gives no activity measurements.

title: Vesicular GABA transporter (VGAT) transports β-alanine
finding: Proteoliposomes with purified VGAT took up beta-alanine driven by membrane potential and requiring chloride, and VGAT also promoted chloride uptake with beta-alanine; the Glu213Ala mutant that disrupts GABA and glycine transport also abolished beta-alanine uptake. In vitro reconstituted system only; the organism of the VGAT used is not stated in the abstract (organism assumed mouse/rodent, unverified).

title: Expression and Characterization of CYP4V2 as a Fatty Acid ω-Hydroxylase
finding: Recombinant CYP4V2 was a selective omega-hydroxylase of saturated medium-chain fatty acids, most efficient with myristic acid, and was inhibited at nanomolar concentration by HET0016. In vitro with expressed enzyme; the link to Bietti's crystalline dystrophy is proposed by the authors. The abstract does not name CYP4A11 or CYP4A22 (also in the GPR of the reactions).

title: The Reduction of α-Tocopherolquinone by Human NAD(P)H:Quinone Oxidoreductase: The Role of α-Tocopherolhydroquinone as a Cellular Antioxidant
finding: Purified human NQO1 reduced alpha-tocopherolquinone to the hydroquinone (Km 370 uM, kcat 5.6e3 per min) and did so more efficiently than coenzyme Q10; in CHO cells expressing human NQO1 the hydroquinone formed correlated with NQO1 activity and protected against lipid peroxidation. Purified enzyme plus a hamster cell model; the abstract does not mention CBR1 (also in the GPR).

title: Cholestenoic acids regulate motor neuron survival via liver X receptors
finding: Cholestenoic acids from the bile acid pathway were profiled in mammalian CSF and shown to act on liver X receptors in motor neurons (zebrafish, mouse in vitro and in vivo); patients with CYP7B1 deficiency (SPG5) had excess 3beta-hydroxycholest-5-en-26-oic acid and those with CYP27A1 deficiency (CTX) had low 3beta,7alpha-dihydroxycholest-5-en-26-oic acid in CSF and plasma. The abstract does not describe the individual enzyme steps that MAR01794 and MAR01796 represent, so the support for those reactions is indirect, from the patient metabolite profiles.

title: Molecular Genetics of 3β-Hydroxy-Δ5-C27-Steroid Oxidoreductase Deficiency in 16 Patients with Loss of Bile Acid Synthesis and Liver Disease
journal: The Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism
finding: Twelve different HSD3B7 mutations were found in 15 further patients (13 kindreds) with loss of bile acid synthesis and cholestatic liver disease; ten mutations tested caused complete loss of enzyme activity, so C27 3beta-HSD in the endoplasmic reticulum is needed for bile acid synthesis. The abstract does not name the 7alpha-hydroxycholesterol substrate of MAR01584 specifically.

title: Mitochondrial β-Oxidation of 2-Methyl Fatty Acids in Rat Liver
finding: Coupled rat liver mitochondria and purified enzymes: the trifunctional beta-oxidation complex hydrates, dehydrogenates and cleaves medium- and long-chain 2-methyl-branched substrates, whereas the matrix L-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase and 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase are inactive with them. Rat only; no vitamin E carboxychromanol intermediate was tested, so the use for the tocotrienol rounds is an inference.

title: Adenosine phosphorylase activity as distinct from inosine-guanosine phosphorylase activity in sarcoma 180 cells and rat liver
finding: Argues that an adenosine-phosphorylating activity in sarcoma 180 cells and rat liver is distinct from inosine-guanosine (purine nucleoside) phosphorylase. Nicotinate riboside is not among the substrates, so the paper does not support nicotinate riboside phosphorolysis by PNP (cited as a reference of MAR04662).

title: Model-based assessment of mammalian cell metabolic functionalities using omics data
finding: Presents CellFie: curated and standardized lists of metabolic tasks of mammalian cells, with gene sets per task derived from genome-scale models and a scoring of omics data on them, applied to transcriptomes from single cells to tissues. Source of the CellFie task numbering and definitions (for example tasks 7, 21, 22, 64, 82, 90, 107, 130, 148, 161, 169, 178, 184, 187) that the drafts correct; the task list itself was not checked beyond the abstract.

title: Functional identification of a vesicular acetylcholine transporter and its expression from a “cholinergic” gene locus.
finding: Rat VAChT expressed in CV-1 cells gave proton-dependent, vesamicol-sensitive acetylcholine accumulation. Stoichiometry was not measured; rat protein only.

title: Cutaneous expression of cytochrome P450 CYP2S1: individuality in regulation by therapeutic agents for psoriasis and other skin diseases
finding: RT-PCR in skin of 27 healthy volunteers and 29 psoriasis patients: CYP2S1 is expressed in skin with large individual variation and is induced by UV, PUVA, coal tar and all-trans retinoic acid. The abstract reports regulation of expression, not metabolism of retinoic acid by the enzyme; the claim that CYP2S1 metabolises retinoate is not stated in the abstract and the full text was not read.

title: Stoichiometry of hydrogen ion-linked dopamine transport in chromaffin granule ghosts
finding: Bovine chromaffin granule ghosts take up dopamine with a stoichiometry of two H+ per dopamine. Other amines and acetylcholine are covered only by analogy; not human.

title: The metabolites NADP+ and NADPH are the targets of the circadian protein Nocturnin (Curled)
finding: NOCT converts NADP+ to NAD+ and NADPH to NADH in vitro (Fig. 1c, 2a). Overexpressed full-length tagged NOCT in A549 cells localised to mitochondria; only a construct lacking the mitochondrial targeting sequence was cytosolic (Fig. 3c-d), so the paper gives no evidence for native cytosolic NOCT. The authors mention only as a possibility that NOCT may also act outside mitochondria.
locator: Results: NOCT activity, mitochondrial localisation; Fig. 1c, 2a, 3c-d

title: Dephosphorylation of 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate by MIPP expands the regulatory capacity of the Rapoport–Luebering glycolytic shunt
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Dictyostelium, bird and mammalian MIPP1 (MINPP1) hydrolyses 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate by removing the 3-phosphate, a route that bypasses 3-phosphoglycerate, unlike BPGM, which removes the 2-phosphate. Erythrocyte MIPP1 activity at 37 C was 0.6 mmol per litre of cells per hour, similar to published BPGM phosphatase estimates. Abstract only; the 2-phosphatase activity of BPGM is background in this paper.

title: Identification of the GalNAc Kinase Amino Acid Sequence
finding: Identifies the GalNAc kinase sequence (pig enzyme, human GALK2 cDNA). The enzyme also phosphorylates galactose, with a Km of about 4 mM for the pig enzyme, and the human cDNA rescued a gal1 yeast mutant, so GALK2 has some galactokinase activity besides being the GalNAc kinase.

title: Generation, Release, and Uptake of the NAD Precursor Nicotinic Acid Riboside by Human Cells
finding: Purified recombinant human cytosolic 5'-nucleotidases CN-II (NT5C2) and CN-III (NT5C3A), but not CN-IA (NT5C1A), dephosphorylate NMN and NAMN in vitro, at millimolar substrate concentrations. Overexpression of CN-II and CN-III in HEK293 and HepG2 cells formed and released nicotinic acid riboside; untransfected HeLa cells release NAR and NR.

title: Nicotinamide Riboside and Nicotinic Acid Riboside Salvage in Fungi and Mammals
finding: Purified bovine purine nucleoside phosphorylase was about 120 times more active on nicotinic acid riboside than yeast Pnp1 (Table 1, p. 163). Human PNP was not tested on this substrate, so the paper supports the activity for bovine PNP only.

title: Kinetic analysis of human CYP24A1 metabolism of vitamin D via the C24-oxidation pathway
finding: Partially purified human CYP24A1 in a phospholipid-vesicle system metabolised 1,25(OH)2D3 and C24-pathway intermediates (Km 0.34 to 15 mmol per mol phospholipid, kcat up to 34 per min). Side-chain cleavage of 24-oxo-1,23,25(OH)3D3 was the most efficient step and gave 1-hydroxy-23-oxo-tetranor-D3, not 1,23-dihydroxy-tetranor-D3, as primary product; the abstract does not state the fate of the C4 product or calcitroic acid formation.

title: Recent Advances in Carrier-Mediated Intestinal Absorption of Water-Soluble Vitamins
finding: Review of carrier-mediated intestinal absorption of water-soluble vitamins (ascorbate, biotin, folate, riboflavin, thiamin, pyridoxine), covering driving forces, molecular identity and regulation of the transporters. Cited as a reference of MAR06512 (FAD exchange); the abstract does not mention FAD transport and the four genes of that reaction are not transporters.

title: Cloning of Human 25-Hydroxyvitamin D-1α-Hydroxylase and Mutations Causing Vitamin D-Dependent Rickets Type 1
finding: cDNA of 25-hydroxyvitamin D 1-alpha-hydroxylase (P450c1alpha) cloned from human keratinocytes; transfected mammalian cells made 1,25(OH)2D3 (HPLC and GC-MS), and keratinocytes of a patient with vitamin D-dependent rickets type 1 lacked the activity and carried frameshift mutations. Vitamin D3 to calcitriol (CellFie task 261).

title: Molecular Cloning of Human Mitochondrial Glycerophosphate Dehydrogenase Gene: Genomic Structure, Chromosomal Localization, and Existence of a Pseudogene
finding: Cloned the cDNA of human mitochondrial glycerophosphate dehydrogenase from an insulinoma library, mapped the gene to chromosome 2q23, worked out its 15-exon structure and found a pseudogene on 19q13.4. It is a gene-structure paper with no enzyme assay or reaction data, so it does not describe the reaction chemistry of MAR00449.

title: The reaction of β-mercaptop0ruvate with lactic dehydrogenase of heart muscle
finding: Title only is available (Europe PMC has no abstract); it reports a reaction of 3-mercaptopyruvate with lactate dehydrogenase from heart muscle. Species and isoenzyme are not stated in what was read; the draft cites it for LDHA/LDHB-type enzymes only, so it does not show the reaction for LDHC or LDHAL6A.

title: In vitro biosynthesis of 3-mercaptolactate by lactate dehydrogenases
organism: Rattus norvegicus;Gloeobacter violaceus;Escherichia coli;Corynebacterium glutamicum;Bacillus cereus
finding: Purified recombinant bacterial lactate dehydrogenases were tested for reduction of 3-mercaptopyruvate to 3-mercaptolactate, with rat liver LDH as comparator: the Gloeobacter enzyme reached 63.6 U/mg (about twice the rat enzyme) and the E. coli, C. glutamicum and B. cereus enzymes had little or no activity. The rat liver LDH is described as active on 3-mercaptopyruvate; no human LDH was tested.

title: Carnitine biosynthesis. beta-Hydroxylation of trimethyllysine by an alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent mitochondrial dioxygenase.
finding: Rat liver mitochondria hydroxylated trimethyllysine to 3-hydroxy-trimethyllysine with alpha-ketoglutarate, Fe2+ and ascorbate, while microsomal and soluble fractions had no activity; the product was cleaved by serine hydroxymethyltransferase to gamma-butyrobetaine aldehyde and glycine. The preliminary digitonin data in the paper point to the outer rather than the inner mitochondrial membrane, so the matrix site rests on UniProt, not on this paper; rat only.

title: Dopamine-Derived Salsolinol Derivatives as Endogenous Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitors: Occurrence, Metabolism and Function in Human Brains
finding: Review which states that the (R) enantiomers of salsolinol derivatives predominate in human brain and are made by an enzyme, (R)-salsolinol synthase, not by the non-enzymatic Pictet-Spengler condensation. The review gives no gene for the synthase and does not itself report the primary assay.

title: Catalytic Function of Nongastric H,K-ATPase Expressed in Sf-21 Insect Cells
finding: Human ATP12A (nongastric H,K-ATPase alpha subunit) co-expressed with the gastric beta subunit (ATP4B) in Sf-21 insect cell membranes gave an active K+-stimulated ATPase (Km for K+ about 116 uM) that is partly inhibited by ouabain; neither protein alone gave activity. Heterologous expression in insect cells only.

title: One substrate many enzymes virtual screening uncovers missing genes of carnitine biosynthesis in human and mouse
finding: Docking of a substrate to AlphaFold models of vitamin B6 enzymes, followed by experimental testing, showed that SHMT1 and SHMT2 catalyse the hydroxytrimethyllysine aldolase step of carnitine biosynthesis; a mouse threonine aldolase (Tha1) that humans lack does it more efficiently. The authors suggest that SHMT activity partly makes up for this gene loss in humans.

title: A catechol-O-methyltransferase that is essential for auditory function in mice and humans
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Positional cloning in mice identified a previously unannotated catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT2) whose missense mutation causes deafness and vestibular defects and lowers enzyme activity; a nonsense mutation in the human ortholog causes nonsyndromic deafness. The paper establishes the gene and its methyltransferase function; it says nothing about Ensembl identifiers in Human-GEM.
